title: Chaos-resilient VPC runtime orchestrator for hot-swap upgrades and deterministic rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a hardened orchestrator for private (VPC) data-plane runtime upgrades that performs a preflight Terraform dry-run, orchestrates a blue/green-like hot-swap without global downtime, and guarantees deterministic rollback under partial failure modes. This ticket implements a 'chaos-resilient' control loop: preflight validation, traffic fencing, incremental worker pool cutover, KV priming probe, and automated rollback gates driven by health checks and cost/latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform preflight plan reports zero destructive changes for control-plane resources unless explicitly requested
Automated cutover completes with no 5xx spikes above 1.5x baseline latency for 95th percentile during a staged rollout (observed across 3 distinct private tenants)
Rollback triggers within 2 minutes of failing health gates and returns the data plane to the previous runtime version without state loss
All automation runs against a staging VPC that mimics customer topologies using the infra-private modules and a deterministic test harness
Runbook and one-click rollback documented in Confluence with links to the Terraform state snapshot and GitHub PRs
plan: Create IaC preflight module: terraform module 'vpc_upgrade_preflight' to validate provider quotas, AMI compatibility, and network CIDR collisions
Implement orchestrator controller (k8s operator/standalone service) that sequences: create blue pool, drain old pool, health-verify new pool, swap routing, and deprovision old pool
Add probe types: synthetic inference queries, KV checksum/latency, and TCP readiness (backend handshake) and expose them as independent health gates
Instrument traffic fencing primitives: per-tenant routing policies + connection-level fencing to prevent cross-tenant session bleed during switchover
Integrate with Terraform pipeline: run plan-only preflight, create explicit state snapshot tag, then apply via an approval step or the operator's IaC bootstrapper
Implement circuit-breaker and backoff: progressive cutover windows (5%, 20%, 60%, 100%) with automated rollback on gate failure
Create test harness that runs fault injection (pod kill, synthetic latency, partial KV corruption) and validates rollback determinism
Author runbook, operator CLI commands for emergency revert, and add dashboard panels in Console for the rollout
risks: Terraform drift between customer-managed resources and operator-driven changes could cause failed rollbacks
Priming KV caches at scale may generate transient load spikes and incorrectly trigger health gates if not rate-limited
Network ACLs and private topology variations across customers may require feature flags per-tenant
Automated rollback during noisy neighbor events may flip versions repeatedly unless hysteresis is tuned
test_plan: Stage: deploy orchestrator to a staging VPC with 3 tenant topologies and run full preflight (quota, AMI, network)
Canaryless progressive validation: perform 4-step progressive percentage routing and assert latency/5xx SLOs at each step
Chaos tests: k8s pod kills, simulated KV latency, and transient network partitions during cutover
Rollback validation: induce a health gate failure at step 20% and verify rollback completes within 2 minutes and no sessions are orphaned
Post-mortem readiness: verify observability events, traces, and Terraform state snapshots are created and stored
observability_checks: Create rollout dashboard: per-tenant P50/P95/P99 latency, 5xx rate, new-pool readiness ratio, and priming throughput
Trace waterfall for a sampled request to verify there are no duplicate token charges or K/V mismatches during switchover
Alerting: create SLO-based alert that escalates to SRE on >2 consecutive gate failures within a 15-minute window
Audit: log every state snapshot creation and operator-driven Terraform apply with run id
rollback_procedure: Operator detects gate failure -> mark new pool as quarantined and stop forwarding new connections
Replay in-flight connection handoff: drain new pool connections while re-enabling old pool listeners; use session affinity window to avoid split-brain
Trigger Terraform revert: apply state snapshot tagged before the cutover (automated step via CI/CD)
Verify KV/priming consistency using checksum comparison and synthetic queries before marking rollback complete
Post-rollback: run a stability window (10 minutes), collect metrics, and create release note with root-cause analysis
notes: We intentionally avoid a full global DNS swap; instead we use tenant-scoped routing to minimize blast radius
The operator will own temporary IAM creds to perform targeted terraform applies; credentials issuance is audited
Consider adding a feature flag for customers that require 'no-operator' mode where we only emit the plan and let customers apply
We will iterate on probe thresholds after initial runs; default values are conservative to reduce false positives
